source.title: On Some Open Problems in Monotonic and Conservative Learning

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an indexed family of languages over the natural numbers, meaning a class of languages for which membership in each language can be effectively decided from its index, with the following separation property for learning from informants? An informant supplies membership information for every natural number, and a learner succeeds when its sequence of indices for languages stabilizes to a correct index for the target language. A learner is strongly monotonic when the languages denoted by its later conjectures always contain the languages denoted by its earlier conjectures. An iterative learner is one whose next conjecture depends only on its previous conjecture and the latest datum. Is there such an indexed family that is strongly monotonically identifiable from informant by some algorithmic learner, but is not strongly monotonically identifiable from informant by any iterative learner, even when the iterative learner may choose its hypothesis space? A stronger positive form asks for the successful learner to use a class-preserving hypothesis space, so that its hypotheses denote only languages from the learned class.
accepted.context_brief: strong monotonicity versus iterative informant learning

evidence.quote: Lange and Zeugmann [LZ92] asked whether there exists an indexed family which can be strongly monotonically identified by a learner from informant, but which cannot be strongly monotonically identified by an iterative learner from informant.

We show that there exists an indexed family which can be strongly monotonically identified using a class preserving hypothesis space but cannot be strongly monotonically identified by an iterative learner, even if the iterative learner is free in the choice of the hypothesis space used.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an indexed family of languages over the natural numbers with the following property for learning from texts? A text for a language contains all and only the elements of the language, presented one at a time in arbitrary order with repetitions allowed. A learner succeeds when its sequence of language-index hypotheses stabilizes to a correct index. A conservative learner changes its conjecture only when the data seen so far contradict the current hypothesis. Is there an indexed family that can be learned from texts with only a bounded number of mind changes, in fact with at most two mind changes, but cannot be learned conservatively from texts?
accepted.context_brief: bounded mind changes versus conservative text learning

evidence.quote: Lange and Zeugmann [LZ93] asked whether there exists an indexed family which can be learned from texts using only a bounded number of mind changes, but cannot be conservatively learned from texts.

In this paper we answer this question positively by showing that there exists an indexed family which can be learned from texts using at most two mind changes, but which cannot be conservatively learned.
